lockStatusAuthority: the frozen ProblemDefinition of the attempt (experiments/poisson2d/problems/)
schemaNote: Applicability-annotated specification of the 2D manufactured Poisson problem. Fields that this problem does not carry are marked NOT_APPLICABLE with a reason; fabricating a value to pass completeness would be a Gate 1 FAIL. Exactly three fields are NOT_APPLICABLE: initialConditions, dimensionalForm, referenceScales.
evidenceLevelReason: An exact closed-form solution exists and is verifiable by substitution; this is the highest evidence level in Article 2.

title.value: Two-dimensional manufactured Poisson equation on the unit square with homogeneous Dirichlet boundaries

scientificQuestion.value: The question under test is not whether a PINN can fit sin(pi x) sin(pi y). It is whether the Leo AI scientific governance, diagnosis, blind-validation and reproduction machinery, validated at C2 on the 1D calibration, carries to a genuinely two-dimensional PDE without distortion: sample identity in 2D, component-separated second-order automatic differentiation, spatial error structure, 2D physics identities, blind claim sets on tensor grids, Tier-1 perturbations whose applicability is re-judged for 2D, and an independent-environment reproduction.

value.type: linear second-order elliptic boundary value problem
value.wellPosedness: Determined: one second-order elliptic PDE with Dirichlet data on the whole boundary of a bounded Lipschitz domain has a unique classical solution (Article 6-1).

value.parameterization: u_theta(x,y) = x (1 - x) y (1 - y) N_theta(x,y)
value.enforcementReason: The 1D calibration established hard enforcement as a validated method at C2 for homogeneous Dirichlet data. Freezing it here isolates the dimension lift: soft-versus-hard is not a variable of this experiment.

initialConditions.reason: the problem is steady; there is no time variable

dimensionalForm.reason: the problem is posed dimensionless by construction

referenceScales.reason: no nondimensionalization is applied, so there are no reference scales to declare

value.verification: -(u*_xx + u*_yy) = 2*pi^2*sin(pi*x)*sin(pi*y) = f; u* vanishes on all four edges. Verified machine-wise in Gate 2a on the registered D_phys and boundary nodes.

closedFormConstants.dirichletEnergy: int int |grad u*|^2 dA = int int f u* dA = pi^2/2
closedFormConstants.boundaryFlux: closed boundary flux of the outward normal derivative = -8

value.symmetry: u*(x,y) = u*(y,x) and u*(x,y) = u*(1-x,y) = u*(x,1-y); the swap symmetry is evidence (PH4), never a training constraint. A symmetric manufactured solution cannot by itself discriminate an x/y swap in the residual operator, which is why Gate 3 carries the asymmetric probe check T2.

secondary.scheme: five-point second-order finite differences, matrix-free conjugate gradients, refinement sequence 8/16/32/64, observed order p in [1.8, 2.2]
secondary.role: implementation sanity cross-check only; it never replaces the analytic reference

value.registry: pinn/governance/poisson2d_contract.py (values, thresholds, levels and the per-criterion dimension verdict and threshold source)
value.frozenBefore: the claim pool was sealed and before any formal run; sources recorded per criterion (PART 10)

value.claimGridFamily: {tensor Gauss-Legendre of order n on (0,1)^2} union {interior tensor Chebyshev-Gauss-Lobatto of count m}
value.boundarySet: Gauss-Legendre nodes of order 32 along each of the four edges, arc-length weights summing to the perimeter 4; spec-known boundary coordinates, identity-exempt (protocol L1)
value.claimIdentity: sampleSetHash = canonical_sha256(sorted(sample identities)); a claim set burns by its samples, not by its artifact bytes
value.derivatives: first and second order by automatic differentiation, components evaluated separately (u_xx and u_yy never only as their sum)
value.precision: float64 throughout; deterministic algorithms; the thread count is part of the frozen configuration
